Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

q-332776.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)-4\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-4L\{1\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-3=2{X}_{1}(s)-\frac{4}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-0={X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\},$ and we have used the fact that $L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-3 & =2{X}_{1}(s)-\frac{4}{s} \\ (s-2){X}_{1}(s) & =3-\frac{4}{s} \\ (s-2){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{3s-4}{s} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{3s-4}{s(s-2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s) & ={X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-1){X}_{2}(s) & ={X}_{1}(s) \\ (s-1){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{3s-4}{s(s-2)} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{3s-4}{s(s-1)(s-2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system  in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{3s-4}{s(s-2)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3s-4}{s(s-1)(s-2)}.
$$

\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-2=4{X}_{1}(s)-\frac{3}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+1=-{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\},$ and we have used the fact that $L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s)+1 & =-{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-2){X}_{2}(s) & =-{X}_{1}(s)-1 \\ (s-2){X}_{2}(s) & =-(\frac{2s-3}{s(s-4)})-1 \\ (s-2){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-(2s-3)-s(s-4)}{s(s-4)} \\ (s-2){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-2s+3-{s}^{2}+4s}{s(s-4)} \\ (s-2){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-{s}^{2}+2s+3}{s(s-4)} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-{s}^{2}+2s+3}{s(s-2)(s-4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2s-3}{s(s-4)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-{s}^{2}+2s+3}{s(s-2)(s-4)}.

q-333128.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}-\frac{2}{s}\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\}-2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & ={e}^{2\cdot t}-2\cdot 1 \\  & ={e}^{2t}-2 \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{-\frac{2}{s-2}+\frac{1}{s-3}+\frac{3}{s}\} \\  & =-2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\}+{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\}+3\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & =-2{e}^{2\cdot t}+{e}^{3\cdot t}+3\cdot 1 \\  & ={e}^{3t}-2{e}^{2t}+3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t}-2 \\ {e}^{3t}-2{e}^{2t}+3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
